question.text: A Cat III AIF scheme closes with commitments of Rs. 1000 crore and has called Rs. 650 crore. Dry Powder = ?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook example uses Rs. 1000 crore of committed capital and Rs. 650 crore of drawn/invested capital, giving dry powder of Rs. 350 crore. Dry powder is therefore committed capital minus capital already called and invested. The Trap: Rs. 1000 crore is the total commitment, Rs. 650 crore is the capital already invested, and Rs. 0 ignores the undrawn portion. None of these is the dry-powder figure. Note: The Rs. 1000 / Rs. 650 / Rs. 350 crore dry-powder illustration is taken from the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
